scores.reason: Measure types: fasting-based (HOMA-IR, fasting insulin) and post-load (OGTT-derived estimates). Insulin immunoassays are widely available but not standardized: among-assay CV 12-66% (median 24%), a common reference preparation did not harmonize them, and there is no insulin reference measurement procedure; the EASL guideline itself says standardized assays are needed. Fasting protocol is simple, OGTT adds a timed protocol. Data are mostly from an older assay generation (2007 ADA workgroup), so confidence is capped at medium.
sources: EASL-EASD-EASO 2024 MASLD guideline PMIDs 38851997, 38852583, 38869512 (project files, usecases-verified.md row 14)

scores.reason: Measure type: C-peptide (fasting or MMTT-stimulated). Immunoassays are on all major US platforms, but all are traceable to WHO 84/510 and still disagree (mean bias up to 36.6% between two platforms; recalibration with matrix-appropriate serum reduced the disagreement). The stimulated option needs a timed MMTT. C-peptide is unstable if serum or plasma is left unspun at room temperature (about -46% to -74% at 48 h). No type 3c cutoff exists to standardize against.

Measure type: C-peptide (serum, glucose/C-peptide ratio, urinary C-peptide/creatinine ratio, UCPCR). Serum C-peptide is widely available but unstandardized across platforms (see row 9). UCPCR is a less common send-out style test, and renal clearance of C-peptide (about half) is an interpretive confounder that no assay can remove; correction methods are described as poorly validated. UCPCR evidence is from one small cohort. Alternative: 1 if only UCPCR counts as the measure.

scores.reason: Measure types: fasting insulin (fasting-based) plus anti-insulin-receptor antibody and genetic testing. Fasting insulin is routine, but the antibody has no standard clinical assay (a bridge assay was built at NIH in 2023 as a research method) and genetic testing is a specialised send-out. The JDS >30 uU/mL threshold has no assay named, and insulin assays differ in range and recovery by platform (abstract-level only). Rows with a composite of routine and send-out components score the limiting component.

scores.reason: Measure type: fasting/hypoglycaemia-sample insulin and C-peptide (suppressed values), with IGF-II as the confirmatory send-out. Insulin and C-peptide are widely available, but the interpretive cutoffs depend on the assay: in a prolonged-fast study, the traditional 36 pmol/L cutoff for non-specific insulin assays did not transfer to a specific ELISA (older-generation data). Needs a critical sample taken at documented low glucose. Suppression is judged at the low end, where platform functional sensitivity matters. Alternative: 3 if only the insulin/C-peptide step is counted; 1 if IGF-II is the measure.

scores.reason: Measure type: C-peptide (fasting serum <0.3 ng/mL, or stimulated <0.5 ng/mL, or urinary <10 ug/day). A single fasting serum C-peptide at onset is a routine immunoassay on US platforms, so 3. The cutoffs sit at the low end, where the platform-to-platform bias (largest at higher concentrations) matters least, but functional sensitivity at 0.3 ng/mL was not checked per US platform. Stimulated and 24-h urine options are protocol-heavy and impractical in DKA. Alternative: 2 if the stimulated test is required.

Fasting insulin is widely available but unstandardized (see row 14). No pregnancy-specific insulin assay evaluation or reference interval was found in the screened records, so pregnancy-specific analytical performance is unknown. anchor_issues: D4 anchors 2 vs 3: C-peptide and fasting insulin are standard laboratory tests on US platforms (suggests 3) but are unstandardized across platforms (2 says 'widely available but unstandardized'). Chose 2 where the decision threshold sits in the range where platforms disagree or a timed protocol is needed (rows 9, 14, 28, 35), and 3 for row 46 where the cutoff is low and a single fasting draw is the base case.

Rows 12, 21 and 35 combine a routine assay with a send-out component (antibody, IGF-II, GCK genetics). The anchors do not say whether to score the limiting component or the main one. Chose: row 12 limiting component (1); rows 21 and 35 the insulin/C-peptide component (2), with the alternative in the reason.
Row 35 mixes a glucose-based trigger (a) and an insulin-based use (b); scored (b).
